title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 188 (Extent of agent’s authority)

content.overview: Section 188 provides that an agent having an authority to do an act has authority to do every lawful thing which is necessary in order to do such act. An agent having an authority to carry on a business has authority to do every lawful thing necessary for the purpose, or usually done in the course, of conducting such business.
content.glance: An agent authorised to do an act has authority to do every lawful thing necessary to do that act. An agent authorised to carry on a business has authority to do every lawful thing necessary for the purpose, or usually done in the course, of conducting that business.
content.study: An agent having an authority to do an act has authority to do every lawful thing which is necessary in order to do such act. An agent having an authority to carry on a business has authority to do every lawful thing necessary for the purpose, or usually done in the course, of conducting such business. Current-law framing: authority includes necessary incidental acts and acts usual in the course of the authorised business.

sections.heading: Authority to do an act
sections.body: An agent having an authority to do an act has authority to do every lawful thing which is necessary in order to do such act.

sections.heading: Authority to carry on a business
sections.body: An agent having an authority to carry on a business has authority to do every lawful thing necessary for the purpose, or usually done in the course, of conducting such business.

examples.title: Necessary incidental acts
examples.body: An agent authorised to sell goods has authority to do every lawful thing necessary to effect the sale under Section 188.

hypotheticals.question: An agent is authorised to carry on a business. Does the authority include acts usually done in the course of that business?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Section 188 provides that an agent having authority to carry on a business has authority to do every lawful thing necessary for the purpose, or usually done in the course, of conducting such business.

distinctions: Extends the express or implied authority under Sections 186–187 by necessary or usual incidents.

distinctions.title: Scope of Section 188
distinctions.body: Section 188 applies only to the circumstances described in its statutory text. It does not create additional grounds or remedies beyond those stated.
